MRK.rationale: MRK presents a rare case of near-full alignment across all three pillars on the short side. Pillar 1 (fundamental health & trajectory): Earnings have collapsed — Q1 2026 EPS of -$1.72 vs. +$2.01 a year ago, operating income swung from +$5.90B to -$3.53B, and net margin halved from ~27% to 13.6%. The GAAP loss is driven by a large one-time acquisition charge (Cidara, ~$9B per the earnings call), but even stripping that out, the underlying trajectory is concerning: Gardasil declined 22%, the Keytruda patent cliff (late 2028/2029) looms with 46% of revenue at risk, and balance sheet equity eroded $5.98B in two quarters. The only genuine positive is $3.92B quarterly OCF, confirming the core business still generates cash. Pillar 2 (valuation): P/E of 35.3x is at the absolute ceiling of its 365-day range (11.1x–35.8x), P/B of 6.87x is near its 7.0x ceiling, and the stock has rallied ~66% from its 365-day low to $127.63 — all while profitability has deteriorificantly deteriorated. The market is pricing an aggressive earnings recovery that the supplied data cannot confirm. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): Q2 2026 earnings on Aug 4 are expected to show EPS of ~$1.36, down 36.2% YoY, with further acquisition-related charges likely. This is a near-term downside catalyst, not an upside one. The combination of collapsing earnings, extreme valuation multiples at range ceilings, a structural Keytruda patent cliff risk, and a negative near-term earnings event creates a strongly negative risk-reward profile.
